cases.question: The forks on my pallet truck are bent. What do I do, who needs to know, and what do I put in the log?

judge.reason: Fully correct: covers stopping use, safe parking, Do Not Use — Faulty tag, no self-repair, telling the FLM straight away, logging the same shift with the SOP-IR-01 details, and FLM escalation to maintenance and the Senior FLM.

answer.answer: Bent forks mean the pallet truck has failed its check. Stop using it straight away, do not work around the fault, and do not try to repair it. Tell your FLM and log it the same shift.
steps: Stop using the pallet truck straight away. Do not work around the fault.
Record the failed check on the Pre-Use Equipment Checklist.
Park it safely: forks fully lowered, out of aisles and clear of fire exits and emergency lanes. If it is a powered truck, switch it off and remove the key.
Attach a 'Do Not Use — Faulty' tag stating the fault (bent forks), the date, and who found it.
Do not attempt any repair yourself. Repairs are done by maintenance.
Tell your FLM straight away. If your FLM is unavailable, go to the Senior FLM.

Log the faulty equipment in the incident system (or paper log if the system is down) the same shift. Record what happened, where, when, who was involved, and the action taken (equipment tagged and taken out of use).

The FLM reports the fault to maintenance and escalates to the Senior FLM the same shift, as the equipment is out of service. Only maintenance or the repairing engineer can remove the tag once the repair is confirmed.
